description: Enforce a mandatory stop-and-summarize checkpoint after the first successful GPU benchmark run. The user's instruction: 如果在h200 / b300一旦跑成功过一次，记得停一下，做一下总结 (once a run on H200 or B300 succeeds even once, stop and produce a summary). Today nothing enforces that: scripts/run-staged.sh ends a successful full stage by printing the next command, so an unsupervised session could keep burning $26.67/hr chasing the next recipe while the one result worth reporting sits unsummarised in S3. This feature makes the stop mechanical rather than a matter of remembering: the runner detects a first success on GPU hardware, records it in the ledger, refuses further paid GPU stages until the summary exists, and provides a generator that turns the run into a written summary. Depends on FEAT-001 through FEAT-003, all complete. Launches nothing and bills nothing.

Bump the schema string and make the loader tolerate the older entries FEAT-003 already writes rather than crashing on them. The plumbing stage on c5d.large has no GPU and must never set gpu_success.

In scripts/run-staged.sh, replace the 'next stage' hint printed after a successful full stage with a prominent STOP notice: state that a GPU benchmark has succeeded, that per the operator's standing instruction the loop stops here, print the RUN_ID and the S3 prefix, and print the two exact commands to run next (scripts/collect-results.sh --run-id <RUN_ID> then scripts/summarize-run.sh --run-id <RUN_ID>). Do not print any further launch command. Determining success must not rely only on the launcher's exit code: also require that status.json for that RUN_ID reached phase=completed, which the launcher's --wait mode already retrieves and which collect-results.sh can fetch from s3://<bucket>/runs/<RUN_ID>/logs/status.json. If the phase cannot be determined, treat it as not-yet-successful and say so rather than claiming a success.

Add the enforcement gate to scripts/run-staged.sh: when the ledger contains an entry with gpu_success true and summary_done false, any subsequent attempt to run a paid GPU stage (gpu-smoke or full) must refuse with a distinct non-zero exit code separate from the CONFIRM_SPEND refusal (use 3, since 2 already means 'refused for want of CONFIRM_SPEND' and 1 means error). The refusal message must name the RUN_ID that is awaiting a summary and print the command that clears the gate. Provide an explicit override flag --ack-summary (or SUMMARY_ACK=yes) for the case where the operator consciously wants to continue, and log loudly in both the output and the ledger when the override is used, so skipping the summary is possible but never silent. Note in the code comment that this gate deliberately fires BEFORE the CONFIRM_SPEND gate, so the stop cannot be bypassed just by supplying CONFIRM_SPEND=yes.

Create scripts/summarize-run.sh in the established house style (`#!/usr/bin/env bash`, `set -euo pipefail`, banner, all-caps `VAR="${VAR:-default}"` config block, `usage()` heredoc with Chinese help text, `while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]` parser, `log()` helper, `trap cleanup EXIT`). Given --run-id it reads the artefacts the run already produced - s3://<bucket>/runs/<RUN_ID>/logs/{status.json,bootstrap.log,gpu.csv,sglang-server.log} and the collected results/<prefix>.json that scripts/collect-results.sh writes - and generates docs/run-summaries/<RUN_ID>-summary.md. Reuse collect-results.sh's JSONL loader and key normalisation (median_tpot_ms is P50, p95_tpot_ms, median_ttft_ms, output_throughput, accept_length) rather than reimplementing them; if that means extracting the loader into a small shared helper both scripts source, do that. Support --fixture so the generator can be exercised against tests/fixtures/ at zero cost with no AWS access, the same way collect-results.sh already does.

The generated summary must contain, and the script must fail loudly rather than emit a placeholder when a value is genuinely unavailable: (1) the configuration actually run - instance type, GPU model, tp size, checkpoint repo with its exact byte total, SGLang image, and the recipe file name, all read from the run's own metadata rather than assumed; (2) the measured numbers against README section 12.1's acceptance targets - TPOT P50 and P95 versus <= 4.5 ms, TTFT P50 and P95 versus <= 1.7 s, E2E P50 versus the 8.45 s derivation in README 12.9 A5, and output tok/s - for both the 40000/1500 customer-load run and the 30000/4096 LMSYS-baseline run; (3) an explicit comparison of the 30000/4096 result against the published baseline README section 12.2 cites, ~266 tok/s = TPOT ~3.76 ms on H200 tp=4 with EAGLE 3/1/4, since reproducing that figure is the stated reason an H200 run has value at all; (4) the observed accept_length against README 12.9 criterion A7, which requires >= 2.0 for speculative decoding to count as effective; (5) GPU utilisation and memory from gpu.csv, summarised as min/mean/max per GPU, which is the telemetry the failed run had none of; (6) wall-clock cost - elapsed time from status.json multiplied by the spot price recorded at launch; (7) a per-criterion PASS/FAIL verdict table covering README 12.9's A1 through A9 with any criterion that cannot be evaluated from the artefacts marked as not-evaluated and the reason given, never silently as PASS.

The summary must also carry a 下一步 section that is explicit about what is and is not established by a single run: which of the README 12.7 test matrix rows remains unmeasured, that a single run does not establish P95 stability or the section 12.9 A8 requirement of 50 consecutive requests without OOM or crash unless the artefacts actually show it, and what the next candidate configuration would be per the A -> C -> B recipe ordering FEAT-003 recorded in docs/RUNBOOK.md. === HOW SUCCESS IS DETERMINED, AND WHAT AN INDETERMINATE PHASE DOES ===
Success = launcher exit code 0 **AND** status.json phase == 'completed'. Both, not either. The exit code alone is worthless here: 0 only means run-instances succeeded, or that the --wait observation loop ended; the benchmark inside the box could still have died. resolve_final_phase() looks first for the launcher's '运行进入终态: <phase>' line (--wait mode prints it) and falls back to a read-only `aws s3 cp s3://<bucket>/runs/<RUN_ID>/logs/status.json -`. If neither yields a phase it returns 'unknown'.
INDETERMINATE = NOT-YET-SUCCESSFUL, and it is said out loud: the ledger records gpu_success=false with final_phase=<whatever>/unknown and the note '（phase=unknown，不算成功）', and the script prints that the run may still be in flight, how to check status.json by hand, and that the next invocation will refill the phase itself. It never claims a success it cannot prove.
THE GAP THAT WOULD HAVE LEFT, AND HOW IT IS CLOSED: without --wait, status.json does not exist yet at the moment run-staged exits, so a naive implementation would record gpu_success=false forever and the gate would never fire - an unattended session could launch A, not wait, and immediately launch C and B for three times $106. So the gate step first runs ledger_refresh_phases(): for every ledger entry that is mode=real, exit_status=0, stage in (gpu-smoke, full), and has neither gpu_success nor final_phase, it does one read-only `aws s3 cp` of that run's status.json and rewrites the entry truthfully. Set LEDGER_REFRESH=false to make the gate completely offline (the tests use that for hermeticity, except case 19 which exercises the refill on purpose with a case-local aws wrapper). summarize-run.sh also writes the phase back, so the ledger converges on truth from both directions.
Sed note: status.json is parsed with `s/.*"phase"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p` rather than requiring the exact '"phase": "' spacing bench-bootstrap.sh happens to emit. The stricter form silently returned an empty phase against a compact-JSON status file and made the refill look broken - a real trap for anything hand-writing that file.

=== README 12.9: WHAT IS GENUINELY EVALUABLE FROM RUN ARTEFACTS ===
Convention implemented and stated in the summary: A1-A5 are judged on the CUSTOMER-LOAD run (40000 in / 1500 out / concurrency 1), because that is README 12.7's test condition; the 30000/4096 run is reported alongside purely as the LMSYS baseline comparison.
EVALUABLE, and evaluated:
  A1 TPOT P50 <= 4.5 ms, A2 TPOT P95 <= 6.0 ms, A3 TTFT P50 <= 1.7 s, A4 TTFT P95 <= 2.5 s, A5 E2E P50 <= 8.45 s - all straight out of bench_serving via collect-results.sh's normalisation (median_* IS the P50).
  A7 accept_length >= 2.0 - bench_serving emits accept_length directly. If the key is absent entirely the verdict becomes 未评估, never PASS.
NOT EVALUABLE from the artefacts, and why:
  A6 整机 8 卡 - the only machine-readable evidence is gpu.csv's distinct index count vs tp_size. When tp == gpu count it is a PASS. On the canonical H200 target it is tp=4 on an 8-GPU box, so the summary reports '没有拆成多副本（符合不拆副本），但 tp=4 只用了 8 卡中的 4 卡' and marks it 未评估 pending human/customer confirmation. It also notes that README 12.7's own P0 row IS H200 tp=4, i.e. the plan and the acceptance wording are in tension - somebody has to decide that, not a script. Without gpu.csv it is 未评估 for lack of any card count at all.
  A8 连续 50 请求无 OOM/crash - completed==num_prompts for both runs plus phase==completed is necessary but not sufficient; proving no OOM/crash needs sglang-server.log / bootstrap.log. The generator scans them for 'CUDA out of memory', 'OutOfMemoryError', 'torch.OutOfMemoryError', 'Segmentation fault', 'CUDA error', 'Traceback (most recent call last)'; a hit is a FAIL, a clean scan with logs present is a PASS explicitly qualified as 'this run only', and missing logs is 未评估. The current fixture has no logs, so A8 is 未评估 there - which is exactly the honest outcome the criterion demands.
  A9 40K vs 4K TPOT < 15% - impossible in principle from README 6.1's two locked commands, which measure 40K and 30K. The summary prints the 40K-vs-30K delta (+12.0% on the fixture) as reference only and marks A9 未评估 with that reason. Getting A9 needs a third bench_serving at --random-input 4000.
So a perfect real run yields at best 6 PASS / 3 未评估 today: A9 needs an extra bench, A8 needs the server log to be present in S3 (bench-bootstrap.sh does stream it, so a real run should upgrade A8 to PASS - the fixture just doesn't carry one), and A6 needs a human ruling on tp=4-on-8-cards.

=== WHAT A FUTURE SESSION NEEDS TO SATISFY THE GATE AFTER A REAL RUN ===
1. Two commands, both zero-spend, both printed by run-staged itself: `bash scripts/collect-results.sh --run-id <RUN_ID> --region us-east-2` then `bash scripts/summarize-run.sh --run-id <RUN_ID> --region us-east-2`. The second one is what flips summary_done and releases the gate.
2. The ledger must exist and contain that RUN_ID, i.e. the run must have been started via run-staged.sh. If a run is launched with launch-bench-ec2.sh directly there is no ledger entry, summarize-run.sh says so and skips the write-back (it still writes the summary), and the gate has nothing to fire on. Start runs through run-staged.sh.
3. The generated summary lands in docs/run-summaries/<RUN_ID>-summary.md and should be committed - it is the human deliverable. The script prints, but deliberately does NOT apply, the two README 12.12.1 / 12.12.2 rows; filling those matrices stays a human review step.
4. Spot price provenance: the cost section prefers the ledger's spot_price_usd_per_hour, which run-staged now records at launch from describe-spot-price-history. Falling back to the built-in reference table (p5en.48xlarge 26.6617 / g6e.xlarge 1.2082 / c5d.large 0.0295) is labelled '参考价，不是本次运行的实际出价'. p6-b300/p6-b200 are NOT in that table, so a B300 run summarised without a ledger entry will show the cost as 未评估 - fine, and better than inventing a price. bench-bootstrap.sh does not record the price on the instance side; if that is ever wanted, the launcher would have to export it into the user-data prelude and write_run_metadata() would have to emit it.
5. Checkpoint byte totals come from a 3-entry table keyed on the repo id (159630041626 / 166898661074 / 294055065805, HF-API-measured). A fourth checkpoint will print '体积未核对' until it is added.
6. If summarize-run.sh exits 1 with '缺少必需的测量值', that run does NOT count as 'succeeded once' in any meaningful sense - do not paper over it with --ack-summary; read sglang-server.log first.

=== DESIGN DECISIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS WORTH KNOWING ===
- gpu-smoke on L40S: the step said to set gpu_success on any successful paid GPU stage and to map g6e.xlarge -> l40s. I do record gpu_success=true for it (the ledger should not lie about the GPU path having worked), but summary_required is computed per family: true for h200/b300/b200, false for l40s. Reason: the operator's instruction is specifically about h200/b300, and blocking the $106 full stage behind a written summary of a $0.30 smoke test would train the operator to type --ack-summary reflexively, which destroys the gate. The gate condition is gpu_success && summary_required != false && !summary_done, and a missing summary_required (old records) defaults to TRUE, i.e. fail-safe.
- --dry-run is warned about but not blocked by the summary gate. It costs nothing, and blocking it would remove the only zero-cost way to validate a recipe change. Documented in RUNBOOK 1.1.
- Exit code 3 is emitted BEFORE the price lookup and before the spend gate, so a gated attempt makes no AWS calls at all (except the optional read-only status.json refill).
- The refusal is itself appended to the ledger with exit_status 3, matching FEAT-003's habit of recording refusals; --ack-summary attempts get summary_ack=true on whatever entry that attempt produces, so 'the override was used' is answerable from the file.
- Reuse over reimplementation: summarize-run.sh does not parse bench_serving output itself. It invokes collect-results.sh --fixture <run dir> --out <scratch> and reads the normalised JSON, tolerating collect's exit 1 (= thresholds missed, values still written) and failing only on >1. So there is exactly one JSONL/median_* implementation in the repo. The only duplicated idiom is the atomic tempfile+os.replace ledger write, which now exists in run-staged.sh (append, set_phase) and summarize-run.sh (mark done); I judged a shared python module not worth introducing a new file layout for ~25 lines. The gpu_family mapping IS duplicated (bash gpu_family_for + a python family_for inside ledger_set_phase, needed because schema/1 records carry no gpu_family); both carry a comment saying change one, change the other.
- Fixtures: gpu.csv for the main fixture deliberately shows 8 H200 cards with 0-3 busy at ~88-98% and 4-7 idle, which is what tp=4 on p5en.48xlarge really looks like and is what makes the A6 discussion concrete. The low-accept variant lives at tests/fixtures/variant-low-accept/ and is named so that it sorts AFTER run-20260807-150955-a1b2: collect-results.sh --fixture tests/fixtures takes `find ... | sort | head -1`, so a directory sorting before it (e.g. anything starting with a letter < 'r') would have silently hijacked pre-existing case 13. Both fixtures carry _fixture_synthetic/_fixture_note, and summaries generated from a fixture get a '本总结基于合成夹具，不是真实测量结果' banner so a fixture-derived summary can never be mistaken for a measurement.
